desc:
A subsequence of a lowercase string is called ideal if for every two neighbouring letters of the subsequence, their positions in the alphabet differ by at most k. For instance, with k = 2, c may be followed by a, b, c, d or e.

Return the length of the longest ideal subsequence of s. The letters need not be different, and the difference 0 is always allowed.

For example, s = "acfgbd" with k = 2 gives 4 (for example a c b d), and s = "abcd" with k = 0 gives 1.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Think of the best ideal subsequence that ends with a particular letter. How does it change when a new character arrives?
Keep dp[x], the length of the longest ideal subsequence seen so far that ends with letter x (26 values).
For a new letter x: dp[x] = 1 + max(dp[y]) over all letters y with |x - y| ≤ k. The answer is the largest dp value at the end.
editorial: A position-by-position DP over pairs of positions would be O(n²). The key observation is that the only thing about a subsequence that matters for extending it is its last letter. So it is enough to remember, for each of the 26 letters, the best length of an ideal subsequence ending in that letter.

When the next character x of s comes, it can extend the best subsequence ending in any letter within distance k of x (including x itself), so the new best length ending in x is one more than the maximum of those values. Updating in place is safe because the new value for x is never smaller than the old one. The answer is the maximum entry. Time O(26 · n), space O(26).
